**Finding: missing (insurance) — redline validated and submitted.**

- **Investigation:** The only occurrence of "insurance" in the Agreement is incidental (in the Net Revenues definition, p0012). There is no insurance section in the outline, and Miscellaneous (§14) ends with Bankruptcy (14.9) and Complete Understanding (14.10).
- **Direction/materiality:** Commerce One is the counterparty vendor and is not merely a licensor — §5.1 gives Corio an on-site full-time operations consultant, §5.2/5.6 add implementation and professional services, and the MarketSite.net Service handles data of Corio and its Customers. That brings the vendor within the rule's scope (data/premises touch), so the absence of insurance is a genuine gap rather than an inapplicable boilerplate omission.
- **Redline:** Inserted a new §14.10 Insurance after p0132 (adjacent to the §8 indemnity structure), at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where Commerce One handles Corio/Customer data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. Since "Customer Data" is undefined in this document, I used "data of Corio or its Customers" to fit the defined terms here.
- **Fallback flagged in the comment:** E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M, consistent with the seed precedent and the low severity of this rule in a licensing-led deal.
